name: Netflix
desc: Subscription video streaming service offering original and licensed series, films, live events and games to consumers worldwide.
markets: Over 300 million paid memberships in more than 190 countries; growing advertising tier and live sports and events programming.
rationale: Global consumer brand already tied to F1 through Drive to Survive; could extend into live content, launches and co-marketing.
f1: Streams the Drive to Survive F1 docuseries, produced with Formula 1's cooperation and licence

name: Apple
desc: Designs iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch and AirPods and sells services such as App Store, Apple Music and Apple TV.
markets: Sells to consumers and businesses worldwide through its own stores, online and carriers in North America, Europe, Greater China and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Already Formula 1's exclusive US broadcaster from 2026 and producer of the F1 film; deeper team or tech partnerships plausible.
f1: Exclusive US broadcaster of Formula 1 on Apple TV from 2026; produced the 2025 film F1

name: Canal+
desc: Pay-television group running Canal+ premium channels, streaming services and the StudioCanal film production and distribution arm.
markets: Subscribers in France, French-speaking Africa, Poland, Vietnam and elsewhere; added South Africa-based MultiChoice in 2025, expanding African reach.
rationale: Long-standing French F1 broadcaster; could deepen with team content, hospitality and promotion in France and Africa.
changed: Separated from Vivendi and listed in London in December 2024; acquired MultiChoice in 2025
f1: Holds the Formula 1 broadcast rights in France

name: Goodman Group
desc: Owns, develops and manages logistics warehouses, industrial estates and data centres for tenants and institutional investment partners.
markets: Operates in Australia, New Zealand, Asia, continental Europe, the UK and the Americas; increasing focus on data centre development.
rationale: B2B property group with global investor base; F1 hospitality could suit investor and tenant relations, but consumer value is low.

name: International Distribution Services
desc: Parent of Royal Mail and GLS, providing letter, parcel and express delivery services to consumers and businesses.
markets: Royal Mail serves the UK; GLS runs parcel networks across Europe and in Canada and the United States.
rationale: Royal Mail is a household UK brand and GLS a pan-European parcel brand; logistics showcase and British GP activation possible.
changed: Acquired by EP Group in 2025 and delisted from the London Stock Exchange

name: Mitsui & Co.
desc: Japanese general trading house investing in and trading energy, metals, machinery, chemicals, food, healthcare and mobility businesses.
markets: Operates in about 60 countries across Asia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Oceania.
rationale: Diversified Japanese group with mobility and energy interests; B2B hospitality possible but no obvious consumer brand to promote.

name: Aramex
desc: Provides express courier, freight forwarding, warehousing and e-commerce fulfilment services for businesses and online shoppers.
markets: Strongest in the Gulf, Middle East and Africa, with operations also in Asia, Europe and Oceania.
rationale: Visible Gulf consumer delivery brand; Middle East Grands Prix (Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Saudi, Qatar) suit regional activation.
changed: Abu Dhabi state-linked investors pursued a takeover offer in 2025; current majority ownership not confirmed

name: JD Logistics
desc: Provides warehousing, express delivery, freight and supply chain technology services to JD.com and external business clients.
markets: Mainly China, with overseas warehouses and logistics operations in Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North America.
rationale: Supports JD's overseas logistics expansion; Chinese GP and international B2B visibility plausible but brand is mostly domestic.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2021

name: United Parcel Service (UPS)
desc: Global package delivery and logistics company offering ground, air express, freight forwarding and supply chain services.
markets: Delivers in more than 200 countries and territories, with largest business in the United States.
rationale: Global logistics brand with strong B2B marketing; F1's worldwide freight and hospitality offer a showcase, though DHL is F1's logistics partner.

name: GXO Logistics
desc: Contract logistics company running warehouses, fulfilment and reverse logistics for retail, e-commerce, consumer and healthcare clients.
markets: Operations mainly in North America and Europe, especially the UK after acquiring Wincanton in 2024.
rationale: B2B logistics brand; hospitality and technology storytelling around automation could work, consumer value limited.
changed: Spun off from XPO in 2021; acquired Wincanton in 2024

name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services
desc: Transportation company providing intermodal, dedicated contract trucking, truckload, final-mile delivery and freight brokerage services.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States, with cross-border services to Canada and Mexico; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: North American B2B freight company; US Grands Prix hospitality possible but little international or brand need.

name: Phillips 66
desc: Refines, transports and markets fuels and chemicals, selling through Phillips 66, Conoco and 76 branded fuel stations.
markets: Mainly United States; also refining and fuel marketing in the UK and parts of Europe.
rationale: Fuel brand with motorsport heritage in the US; F1's US races offer fit, but rivals' lubricant tie-ins are stronger.
changed: Spun off from ConocoPhillips in 2012

name: Wabtec
desc: Makes locomotives, braking, signalling and digital systems for freight railroads and passenger transit operators.
markets: Serves freight and transit customers across North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia.
rationale: Industrial B2B supplier; engineering showcase possible but rail customers make F1 a weak fit.
changed: Acquired GE Transportation in 2019

name: Scan Global Logistics
desc: Freight forwarding group offering air, sea and road freight, contract logistics and project cargo to shippers.
markets: Network of offices in dozens of countries across Europe, Asia, the Americas and Oceania, grown through acquisitions.
rationale: B2B forwarder with little brand profile; motorsport freight or hospitality could be considered, but fit is modest.

name: Tristar Transport
desc: Transports and stores bulk liquids such as fuels, chemicals and lubricants by road, sea and terminal facilities.
markets: Operates across the Middle East, Africa and Asia for oil, gas, chemical and industrial customers.
rationale: B2B liquid logistics firm with low consumer awareness; Gulf race hospitality only a weak reason for F1.

name: Brambles
desc: Rents reusable pallets, crates and containers under the CHEP brand to manufacturers, growers and retailers.
markets: Operates in about 60 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: B2B supply chain group with sustainability story; little consumer brand need, so F1 fit is modest.

name: Flexport
desc: Digital freight forwarder handling ocean, air and truck freight, customs brokerage and trade finance for importers and exporters.
markets: Offices and customers across North America, Europe and Asia, handling cross-border trade worldwide.
rationale: Tech-led logistics brand; F1 could showcase supply chain technology and offer hospitality to shipper clients.

name: inDrive
desc: Ride-hailing app where riders and drivers negotiate fares, also offering delivery, courier, intercity and financial services.
markets: Operates in over 1,200 cities across 48 countries, mainly in Latin America, Africa, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Consumer mobility brand active in sports marketing; F1 races in Latin America and Asia could support awareness.
changed: Founded in Russia as InDriver; rebranded inDrive

name: Kuehne + Nagel
desc: Global logistics provider offering sea freight, air freight, road transport and contract logistics to exporters and manufacturers.
markets: Operates in more than 100 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B logistics brand; hospitality and logistics showcase possible, though DHL holds the F1 logistics role.

name: MTN Group
desc: Mobile network operator offering voice, data, mobile money (MoMo) and enterprise services to consumers and businesses.
markets: Operates in around 16-20 markets, mainly across Africa, including Nigeria, South Africa, Ghana and Uganda.
rationale: Major African consumer brand; F1 has no African race now, but global brand profile and fintech push give moderate fit.

name: SF Express
desc: Express delivery and logistics company offering parcels, freight, cold chain, supply chain and international logistics services.
markets: Largest courier in China; international express and Kerry Logistics give operations across Asia and other regions.
rationale: Leading Chinese delivery brand expanding abroad; Chinese GP activation and international B2B awareness plausible.
changed: Parent S.F. Holding listed in Hong Kong in 2024; acquired control of Kerry Logistics in 2021

name: ID Logistics Group
desc: Contract logistics company providing warehousing, order preparation, transport management and e-commerce fulfilment for retail and industry clients.
markets: Operates around 20 countries in Europe, the Americas and Asia, including the US after buying Kane Logistics.
rationale: B2B logistics firm with modest brand profile; hospitality for retail clients is the main angle, fit is limited.
changed: Acquired Kane Logistics (US) in 2022

name: Hyundai Glovis
desc: Provides car-carrier shipping, finished vehicle logistics, contract logistics and parts distribution, mainly for Hyundai and Kia.
markets: Logistics and shipping operations across Asia, North America, Europe and other regions serving Hyundai Motor Group and others.
rationale: Automotive logistics brand linked to Hyundai group; motorsport logistics fit exists but consumer brand value is low.

name: Thor Industries
desc: Manufactures recreational vehicles under brands including Airstream, Jayco, Keystone, Heartland and, in Europe, Erwin Hymer Group.
markets: Sells mainly in North America and Europe through independent dealer networks.
rationale: Consumer leisure vehicle brands; US races could suit, but RV buyers are a narrow match for F1.
changed: Acquired Erwin Hymer Group in 2019

name: Corning
desc: Materials science company making specialty glass such as Gorilla Glass, optical fibre and cable, ceramics and labware.
markets: Supplies device makers, telecom carriers, data centres, automakers and labs in North America, Asia and Europe.
rationale: Technology materials brand with automotive glass and emissions products; B2B showcase possible but not obvious.

name: James Hardie
desc: Manufactures fibre cement siding, trim and backer board, plus Azek decking, for homebuilders, contractors and homeowners.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States, with operations in Australia, New Zealand and Europe.
rationale: Well-known US builder brand; US Grands Prix could support marketing, but F1 audience fit is moderate.
changed: Acquired Azek in 2025

name: Sika
desc: Makes construction chemicals and industrial products including sealants, adhesives, waterproofing, concrete admixtures, roofing and automotive bonding materials.
markets: Subsidiaries in about 100 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B brand with automotive adhesives business; technology showcase and contractor hospitality give plausible fit.

name: Sandvik
desc: Engineering group making mining equipment, rock tools and metal-cutting tools such as Sandvik Coromant for industry.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Precision machining tools serve automotive and aerospace; engineering showcase possible, but mostly B2B.
changed: Spun off materials unit Alleima in 2022

name: Jobandtalent
desc: Online staffing platform matching temporary and flexible workers with employers in logistics, retail and other sectors.
markets: Operates in several European countries, including Spain, the UK and Germany, and in the United States.
rationale: Staffing rivals Randstad and ManpowerGroup sponsor F1; plausible for employer brand, though budget scale is uncertain.

name: American Tower
desc: Owns and leases wireless towers and communication sites to mobile operators and runs CoreSite data centres.
industry: telecom tower and data centre REIT
markets: Sites in the United States, Latin America, Europe and Africa; sold its India business in 2024.
rationale: B2B infrastructure landlord with few consumer touchpoints; hospitality for carrier clients only, so weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired CoreSite in 2021; sold India business to Brookfield in 2024

name: DayOne
desc: Develops and operates hyperscale data centre campuses, leasing capacity to cloud providers and large internet companies.
markets: Campuses in Asia, including Singapore, Malaysia (Johor), Indonesia and Thailand; further expansion plans not verified here.
rationale: B2B infrastructure developer with little brand need; Singapore GP hospitality for hyperscale clients is the main angle.
changed: Formerly GDS International, the overseas arm of China's GDS; separated and renamed DayOne in 2025

name: Nscale
desc: Builds AI data centres and operates GPU cloud services for AI developers, enterprises and hyperscale partners.
industry: AI data centres and GPU cloud
markets: Operates in Europe, including the UK and Norway, and in the US and Asia, with large GPU deployments for Microsoft.
rationale: Fast-growing AI infrastructure firm; F1 data and technology storytelling could build enterprise awareness, as CoreWeave does.
changed: Spun out of Arkon Energy and founded in 2024

name: NVIDIA
desc: Designs GPUs, AI accelerators, networking and software platforms for data centres, gaming, professional graphics and automotive.
markets: Sells to hyperscalers, enterprises, PC makers and carmakers across North America, Asia-Pacific and Europe.
rationale: Rivals AMD and Qualcomm (Snapdragon) sponsor F1; simulation, AI and automotive tie-ins give a clear technology showcase.

name: AD Ports Group
desc: Develops and operates ports, industrial zones, logistics and maritime services, including Khalifa Port and KEZAD.
markets: Core business in Abu Dhabi, with growing port and logistics operations in Africa, Asia and Europe.
rationale: State-linked Gulf group active in sports sponsorship; Abu Dhabi GP and international expansion give a plausible fit.
changed: Abu Dhabi Ports Company now trades as AD Ports Group; listed in 2022

name: ACS, Actividades de Construcción y Servicios
desc: Construction and infrastructure group building and operating transport, energy, social and data centre projects worldwide.
markets: Operates in North America (Turner), Europe, Australia (CIMIC) and other regions through Hochtief and its own units.
rationale: Global contractor with B2B hospitality needs; Spanish GP and US races could host clients, though brand marketing is light.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone
desc: Operates ports and terminals, including Mundra, plus logistics, rail and marine services for shipping lines and cargo owners.
markets: Mainly India, with terminals abroad including Haifa (Israel), Colombo (Sri Lanka), Dar es Salaam and Australia.
rationale: Part of the Adani Group with international port ambitions; F1 would give B2B visibility, but consumer value is low.

name: Celestica
desc: Electronics manufacturing services company producing networking, server and storage hardware for hyperscalers, plus aerospace and industrial products.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Asia and Europe, serving cloud, communications, aerospace and industrial clients.
rationale: B2B electronics manufacturer with little brand profile; hospitality for hyperscale clients is possible but fit is modest.

name: Cerebras Systems
desc: Makes wafer-scale AI processors and CS-series systems and sells AI inference and training cloud services.
markets: Customers in the US and abroad, including G42 in the UAE and other enterprises, labs and governments.
rationale: AI hardware challenger seeking awareness against larger rivals; F1 speed narrative could suit, but B2B focus limits value.
changed: Withdrew a planned IPO filing in 2025

name: Cloudflare
desc: Provides CDN, DDoS protection, zero trust security, DNS, edge computing and AI inference services to websites and enterprises.
markets: Network in over 300 cities; customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers (CrowdStrike, Zscaler, 1Password) sponsor F1; strong technology tie-in and enterprise hospitality value.

name: Crusoe
desc: Builds and operates energy-focused AI data centres and offers GPU cloud services to AI labs and enterprises.
industry: AI data centres and GPU cloud
markets: Operations mainly in the United States, including the Abilene, Texas campus, with some capacity in Europe.
rationale: Fast-growing AI infrastructure brand; F1 technology storytelling plausible, as CoreWeave shows, but customers are few and large.

name: Envision Group
desc: Makes wind turbines, batteries through AESC and energy storage, and runs green hydrogen and energy management software businesses.
markets: Wind business strong in China, India and other markets; AESC battery plants in Asia, Europe and the United States.
rationale: Already a motorsport sponsor through Formula E's Envision Racing; F1 sustainability narrative could appeal.

name: Equinix
desc: Operates International Business Exchange data centres offering colocation and interconnection to cloud providers, networks and enterprises.
markets: Over 250 data centres in about 70 metros across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global digital infrastructure brand; data and connectivity storytelling and enterprise hospitality make F1 plausible.

name: Shapoorji Pallonji Group
desc: Family-controlled conglomerate in construction and engineering, real estate, infrastructure, water, energy and financial services.
markets: Mainly India, with construction projects in the Middle East and Africa; holds about 18% of Tata Sons.
rationale: Large Indian contractor with Gulf and African projects; B2B hospitality only, little consumer marketing.

name: Snowflake
desc: Cloud data platform letting enterprises store, analyse and share data and build AI applications on major public clouds.
markets: Thousands of enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, sold on consumption pricing.
rationale: Enterprise data rivals (Oracle, SAP, Salesforce) sponsor F1; strong data and AI technology storytelling fit.

name: The Boring Company
desc: Builds underground transport tunnels, including the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop carrying passengers in Tesla vehicles.
markets: Projects in the United States only, mainly Las Vegas; no verified international operations.
rationale: Musk-founded tunnelling firm with Las Vegas presence; little need for sponsorship marketing, weak F1 fit.

name: WSP Global
desc: Engineering and professional services firm providing design, advisory and project management for transport, buildings, water, energy and environment.
markets: Offices in about 50 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global B2B consultancy; client hospitality possible, as AtkinsRéalis does in F1, but brand-led need is limited.

name: Caterpillar
desc: Makes construction and mining equipment, engines, turbines and rail products under the Cat brand, with Cat Financial.
markets: Sells through dealers in nearly every country across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global brand with dealer hospitality needs; rivals JCB and Komatsu sponsor F1, making it a plausible fit.
changed: Moved headquarters to Irving, Texas in 2022

name: ACCIONA
desc: Develops renewable power, infrastructure, water treatment and desalination projects, and runs urban mobility and other services.
markets: Operates in over 40 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Sustainability-led infrastructure brand with motorsport history in Dakar and Formula E; F1 hospitality and green narrative plausible.

name: Baseten
desc: Provides an inference platform for deploying and serving machine learning models for AI startups and enterprises.
markets: Customers mainly US AI-native startups and enterprises; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Young B2B AI infrastructure startup; F1 could raise awareness but budgets and brand need are limited.

name: Fluidstack
desc: Builds and operates large GPU compute clusters and AI data centres for AI labs such as Anthropic.
industry: GPU cloud and AI data centres
markets: Customers and sites in the United States and Europe, including a planned large AI campus in France.
rationale: Fast-growing AI compute provider with few large customers; little brand need, so F1 fit is modest.
changed: Founded in London; now headquartered in New York

name: Huawei
desc: Makes telecom network equipment, smartphones, laptops and wearables and provides cloud, AI chips and smart-car solutions.
markets: Strong in China, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America and parts of Europe; largely shut out of the US.
rationale: Huge consumer brand with car-tech ambitions, but US export restrictions make an F1 tie-up sensitive.

name: Nutanix
desc: Sells hybrid multicloud software and hyperconverged infrastructure for running virtual machines and applications across data centres and clouds.
markets: Enterprise, government and service-provider customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise IT brand competing with VMware; F1 technology storytelling and hospitality plausible, like NetApp and Dell.

name: SambaNova
desc: Makes reconfigurable dataflow AI chips and a full-stack platform and cloud service for running large AI models.
markets: Customers mainly US enterprises, governments and national labs; international deployments not verified.
rationale: Niche B2B AI hardware company; limited brand need and resources make F1 a weak fit.
changed: Reported in 2025 to be in acquisition talks with Intel; outcome not confirmed

name: Stora Enso
desc: Produces packaging board, biomaterials, wooden building products such as CLT, and pulp and paper from forests.
markets: Mainly Europe, with operations and sales in China, the Americas and other regions.
rationale: Sustainability-focused materials group; B2B story around renewable materials possible, but F1 fit is weak.

name: HUMAIN
desc: Saudi AI company building data centres, Arabic AI models such as ALLaM, cloud services and AI applications.
markets: Customers mainly Saudi government and enterprises; announced data centre and chip partnerships with US firms for expansion.
rationale: State-backed brand with global ambitions; Saudi GP and PIF's sports push make F1 a plausible showcase.
changed: Launched by PIF in 2025

name: Modal Labs
desc: Serverless cloud platform letting developers run AI and data workloads on GPUs without managing infrastructure.
markets: Customers mainly US AI companies and developers paying for usage; no verified international operations.
rationale: Young developer-focused cloud startup with a small marketing budget and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Together AI
desc: AI cloud letting developers run, fine-tune and train open-source AI models on GPU clusters via an API.
markets: Customers mainly US AI startups and enterprises; no verified international operations.
rationale: Developer-focused AI cloud with limited consumer brand need; F1 fit weak to moderate.

name: VINCI
desc: Concessions and construction group operating motorways and airports and building infrastructure through VINCI Construction and Eurovia.
markets: Operates in over 100 countries, with airports including Lisbon, Lyon, Gatwick and Kansai.
rationale: Airport and motorway owner with consumer touchpoints; European races and B2B hospitality give a plausible fit.

name: AECOM
desc: Engineering firm providing design, program management and consulting for transportation, water, energy and building projects.
markets: Works for governments and companies in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B consultancy with mainly public-sector clients; hospitality possible but little brand-led need.

name: DriveNets
desc: Develops network operating software for white-box routers used by telecom operators and Ethernet fabric for AI clusters.
markets: Customers include AT&T and other operators in North America, Europe and Asia, plus AI cloud providers.
rationale: Niche B2B networking vendor; Extreme Networks and Cisco show F1 fit, but DriveNets has little brand need.

name: PhysicsX
desc: Builds AI models that simulate physics to speed engineering design for aerospace, automotive, energy and semiconductor manufacturers.
markets: Engineering customers in the UK, Europe and the United States; expanding its US presence.
rationale: Co-founded by former F1 engineer Robin Tuluie; simulation technology is a natural showcase with teams and engineering clients.

name: Rackspace Technology
desc: Provides managed cloud, consulting and security services helping enterprises run applications on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and private clouds.
markets: Customers and offices across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: IT services brand under financial pressure; hospitality for enterprise clients possible, but budget for F1 is doubtful.
changed: Taken private by Apollo in 2016; returned to Nasdaq in 2020

name: thyssenkrupp
desc: Industrial group producing steel, materials distribution, automotive components and naval ships and submarines through TKMS.
markets: Operations and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; strongest in Germany and Europe.
rationale: Supplies automotive components and steel to carmakers; engineering B2B showcase possible, but restructuring limits budgets.
changed: Sold elevator business to private equity in 2020; listed naval unit TKMS in 2025, keeping a majority

name: Fincantieri
desc: Builds cruise ships, naval vessels and specialist offshore ships, and provides ship systems and services.
markets: Shipyards in Italy, the United States, Norway (Vard) and other countries; customers are cruise lines and navies.
rationale: Italian engineering brand serving cruise lines; Italian races and hospitality plausible, but defence work limits fit.

name: Epiroc
desc: Makes rock drilling rigs, underground loaders and trucks, tools, automation software and services for mining and construction.
markets: Customers in about 150 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B mining equipment maker; automation and electrification storytelling possible, but F1 fit is weak.
changed: Spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018

name: Dar Global
desc: Develops luxury branded residential projects, including Trump- and other designer-branded towers, for wealthy international buyers.
markets: Projects in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, the Maldives and Europe; buyers come from many countries.
rationale: Luxury branded property sold to international buyers; Gulf Grands Prix and F1 hospitality suit its audience.
changed: Listed on the London Stock Exchange main market in 2023

name: Digital Realty
desc: Data centre REIT leasing colocation, interconnection and hyperscale space to cloud providers, enterprises and network operators.
markets: Several hundred data centres in about 25 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Digital infrastructure brand with enterprise clients; connectivity storytelling and hospitality make F1 plausible.
changed: Acquired Interxion in 2020

name: Avis Budget Group
desc: Car rental group operating Avis, Budget and Zipcar brands for leisure and business travellers at airports and cities.
markets: Operates in about 180 countries via company-owned and licensee locations, largest in North America and Europe.
rationale: Consumer travel brand with race-weekend rental demand; F1 travel audiences give plausible fit.

name: Blackstone
desc: Alternative asset manager investing in private equity, real estate, credit and hedge fund strategies for institutions and individuals.
markets: Investors and portfolio companies across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Peers such as Carlyle and Goldman Sachs back F1 teams; investor hospitality and wealth marketing give a strong fit.

name: CBRE Group
desc: Commercial real estate services firm offering leasing, sales, property and facilities management, valuation and investment management.
markets: Operates in over 100 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global B2B brand serving corporate occupiers; client hospitality at races worldwide is a plausible use.

name: Simon Property Group
desc: REIT owning and operating malls, Premium Outlets and Mills centres leased to major retailers.
markets: Mainly United States, with outlet interests in Asia, Europe and Canada and a stake in Klépierre.
rationale: US retail landlord with high consumer footfall; US races could support activation, but fit is moderate.

name: FIVE Holdings
desc: Owns and operates FIVE lifestyle hotels and residences, including FIVE Palm Jumeirah and FIVE Zurich.
markets: Hotels and residences in Dubai and Zurich; customers are international travellers and property buyers.
rationale: Nightlife-led hospitality brand; Abu Dhabi GP and F1 party hosting fit its marketing style.

name: ROSHN
desc: Develops large residential communities in Saudi cities, selling homes and community facilities to Saudi families.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia only; no verified international activity.
rationale: PIF-owned brand already title sponsor of the Saudi Pro League; Saudi GP activation plausible, but customers are domestic.

name: Tishman Speyer
desc: Develops, owns and operates office, residential, life science and mixed-use properties, including Rockefeller Center.
markets: Properties in the United States, Europe, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Premium property owner with corporate tenants; B2B hospitality possible, little consumer marketing need.

name: Omniyat
desc: Develops luxury residential and hotel towers in Dubai, including The Opus by Zaha Hadid and One at Palm Jumeirah.
markets: Projects in Dubai; buyers include international high-net-worth investors. No verified projects outside Dubai.
rationale: Ultra-luxury brand targeting wealthy buyers; F1 Paddock Club audiences match, especially at Gulf races.

name: WeWork
desc: Provides coworking spaces, private offices and memberships to freelancers, startups and corporate clients in cities worldwide.
markets: Around 600 buildings in about 125 cities across the Americas, Europe and Asia, some via licensees.
rationale: Recognised brand rebuilding after bankruptcy; limited budget makes F1 sponsorship a weak fit.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2023; emerged in 2024 majority-owned by a Yardi Systems affiliate

name: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield
desc: Owns, develops and operates flagship Westfield shopping centres, plus offices and convention venues in Europe and the US.
markets: Malls in continental Europe, the UK and the United States, with high consumer footfall.
rationale: Consumer-facing mall brand; race-linked activations in malls possible, but marketing budgets are constrained.

name: Property Finder
desc: Online property portal listing homes and offices for sale or rent, earning fees from agents and developers.
markets: Operates in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain and Egypt; no verified expansion beyond MENA.
rationale: Marketing-led Gulf consumer brand; Abu Dhabi, Saudi and Qatar races suit regional activation.

name: Localiza
desc: Rents cars to consumers and companies, runs fleet outsourcing and sells used cars through Seminovos.
markets: Mainly Brazil, with operations in other Latin American countries such as Argentina and Mexico.
rationale: Leading Brazilian mobility brand; São Paulo GP activation could suit, with broader international value limited.
changed: Merged with Unidas in 2022

name: JLL
desc: Commercial real estate services firm offering leasing, capital markets, property and facilities management and investment management.
markets: Operates in about 80 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global B2B brand serving corporate occupiers and investors; client hospitality at races worldwide is plausible.

name: Mitsui Fudosan
desc: Develops and owns offices, LaLaport malls, outlet parks, hotels and condominiums in Japan and abroad.
markets: Mainly Japan, with property in the United States, the UK and Asia.
rationale: Major Japanese property brand; Japanese GP hospitality plausible, though international consumer value is limited.

name: Ayala Corporation
desc: Philippine conglomerate with interests in real estate, banking, telecoms, energy, industrial technology and healthcare.
markets: Mainly the Philippines, with energy and electronics manufacturing operations elsewhere in Asia and abroad.
rationale: Philippines-focused conglomerate; no Philippine race and limited international brand need, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Sobha Realty
desc: Develops and builds luxury residential communities and towers in the UAE, including Sobha Hartland in Dubai.
markets: Projects mainly in the UAE; buyers include international investors. Wider expansion not verified.
rationale: Recognised UAE property brand that sponsors sport and events; Gulf Grands Prix hospitality suits buyer marketing.

name: Binghatti
desc: Develops design-led residential towers in Dubai, including Bugatti Residences, Burj Binghatti Jacob & Co and Mercedes-Benz Places.
markets: Projects in Dubai; apartments sold to local and international buyers. No verified projects outside the UAE.
rationale: Marketing-led developer already licensing car brands; F1 fits its automotive luxury positioning and Gulf buyers.
f1: Licenses the Mercedes-Benz brand (F1 team owner) for its Mercedes-Benz Places towers; no direct F1 deal
